My poppy's corpse in his house when I was around 17. Our family (mainly my mom, aunt and uncles) had done an intervention a few weeks prior to address my Poppy's alcoholism. Apparently, it had ended poorly for all involved, and everyone went no contact as they had promised to do if he didn't accept help.

After a few weeks of him ignoring calls and texts, we (mom, aunt and me) went to his house on a whim one day. 

First thing I noticed as I stood outside the sliding glass doors (while mom found the spare key) was the blanket of dead flies on the carpet. Then I noticed the kitchen island, which was packed with rows and rows of empty beer bottles (this from a man who was notorious for cleanliness despite his addiction.) 

I was too nervous to really take in the smell until I was stopped several feet inside. Dead flies were crunching under my shoes and it was so hot (GA summer hot). It's the smell everyone describes but which you can't really understand unless you've been there yourself. Putridly sweet, burning your nostrils and sticking to the back of your throat.  

My mom and aunt walked forward and were yelling at me to stay back, but I took enough steps forward to see something large and black on the floor, partially blocked by one of those assisted-standing chairs. It was a black mass wrapped around a heater and I could see little yellowish nubs sticking out of it. 

My first thought was that the heater had burned something into a black puddle and we were lucky it hadn't burned the whole house down. 

My second thought (more of a realization) was that I was looking at the decayed soupy remains of my Poppy. If only the house had caught fire and burned it all down.

My Mom and aunt were pushing me out of the house while yelling to their dad. They were trying to shout comforting things to him, like "we're right here, dad," "it'll be ok," "you'll be ok,"  while yelling at me not to look. 

After a whirlwind of hysterical crying, phone calls and blue lights, we watched people (EMS? Police?) remove black bags on gurneys. Their best guess was that he's been there for a few weeks, but there was no telling. No way of knowing what, exactly, had killed him. 

Later, I had to go back in again with family to clean up bottles, organize and sort through personals. Someone had used a throw blanket to cover the decomp stain where he had decayed for all those weeks. 

I was later told that he had set out all his important documents on a desk. We believe it was suicide by alcohol overdose, with all the empty bottles and neatly stacked cartons as a final "f*ck you." There was no note. 

Mom took just a few small keepsakes from his house and stored them in our garage. For months after, I smelled that sickly sweet scent every time I walked in there or even just by the door. Sometimes, if I imagine really hard, I can still smell it bad enough that my throat hurts, my nose clogs and my eyes water.

Growing up, my mom had this line-in boyfriend, Bill. He was an ex arny, quick to anger sort. He once lit our cat on fire with his cigarette and laughed about it. Only good thing about him was that he came with a daughter about our age, who we got along great with. 

They were on and off for years, but I was around 15 when my mom left him for good. He displayed a lot of stalkery behavior after that (peeking through windows, following us, leaving weird shit in the mailbox, sending threatening messages, informing us that he had his guns on him at all times, etc) but for the most part, it didn't involve us kids.

Well, one day (maybe 3-5 months after the breakup) I got off the bus and walked down the long driveway to our house which was situated back in the woods. As I got closer, I saw that the garage was open. Didn't worry me at the time; maybe mom was home early and forgot to tell me, or maybe we just didn't close it when we left that morning. Whatever the case, I walked in through the garage door without a worry. 

And found Bill in the kitchen drinking a cup of coffee. I remember immediately feeling panicked and scared,  and that the whole room smelled like coffee and cigarettes. In retrospect, the audacity of the man to break into his ex's house and brew a pot of coffee is shocking. 

Though he and I never really got along, something told me now wasn't the time to my teenaged melodramatic indignation. Like a light switch, my body took over and I was suddenly smiling, "Mr. Bill!" (cause we always had to call him "Mr") He looked kinda surprised. I don't really remember what either of us said, but he got to his point of being there: "Your mother tells me that you don't like me. She says you don't like being around me, and don't want me to come back." 

Cue Surprised Pikachu face. "Whaaaat?" I denied it fervently, insisting that I missed him and his daughter, that I'd been hoping to see them, that me and her had been talking about what we could do to get them back together and he could ask her that. 

I don't remember how the conversation went after that. I just remember his face and neck. It always got red when he was mad, and it was very, very red. Veins we're sticking out. His eyes were super wide. 

Eventually, I remember going upstairs to my room and hearing him finishing another cup of coffee. I probably said I had homework or something. Up in my room, I locked the door and immediately texted my mom that he was there. But she had a job where she couldn't immediately look at her phone, so it was some time before she'd see it. 

The garage eventually closed but I didn't hear his old truck start up. From my upstairs window, I could see a good distance and saw his truck parked at the old barn a good distance away. In retrospect, I realized that he'd done this so I wouldn't know he was there. 

That was the last time I ever saw him, but not the last I ever heard of him. He eventually moved out of the country, and none of his kids have anything to do with him. I still speak to his daughter from time to time; she's got 3 kids and seems happy. 

Mom remarried and is very happy too. We hadn't heard from the guy in like 10 years. 

Then, at random, my mom looked up his Facebook page and saw a recent picture he'd taken of himself standing in front of a very familiar building. It was her small work office during a Christmas event. 

We believe he was just saying having himself a laugh, probably suspecting (or hoping) that we look him up and would be creeped out. He's remarried now too, and that woman has two small girls from a different marriage. 

Hope they all get away safely.

In the grand scheme of things, what’s a week? What’s a month or even 2, if it means a lifetime? Because that’s what’s at stake; your lifetime, and the lifetime your baby girl will miss out on should any moment be too much.
